title: Can the last digit tell us about fours?
description: Counting in fours builds a strip of numbers, and the video reads the last digit of each one. Twelve and twenty two end in the same digit but only twelve is on the strip, and Keeko's doubt, that any even last digit will do, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: the last digit alone cannot tell whether four divides a number, because twelve and twenty two end in the same digit. Watch for students who carry the rule for two over to four.

source: Look at the multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, ... Are you able to observe any patterns that can be used? Similarly, can we check if a number is divisible by 4 by looking at the last digit?
video_script.why: The child reads the last digits of the count in fours, sees that they are all even, and finds that twelve and twenty two end in the same digit but only one of them is in the count.
video_script.substitution: Count in fours, read the last digits, and test whether a last digit can decide by finding two numbers with the same last digit and different results.
video_script.anchor: a strip of number cards counting in fours from 4, with the last digit of each card lit
video_script.wrong_answer: every number that ends in an even digit is divisible by four
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says every number that ends in an even digit is divisible by four, because the last digits of the count are all even. Six, ten and fourteen end in even digits and are not in the count, so the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: No, the last digit alone cannot decide

final_answer.value: No: the last digit alone does not work; 12 and 22 end in the same digit
final_answer.spoken: no, the last digit alone does not work, because twelve and twenty two end in the same digit

hold_back: Answer: No: the last digit alone does not work; 12 and 22 end in the same digit
never_show: every number that ends in an even digit is divisible by 4
maths_rules: the last digits go 4, 8, 2, 6, 0, 4, 8, 2, so they repeat after five numbers and are all even
12 = 4 x 3 is in the count and ends in 2
22 ends in 2, but the count goes 20, 24, so 22 = 5 x 4 + 2 is not in it
12 and 22 have the same last digit and different results, so the last digit alone cannot decide
6 = 4 + 2, 10 = 2 x 4 + 2 and 14 = 3 x 4 + 2 end in even digits and are not multiples of 4
video_script.design: One idea: the last digit alone cannot decide for four. Assumes the earlier tests for two, five and ten. Wrong idea: any even last digit will do. The strip stays on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks every number that ends in an even digit is divisible by four.
The reason is that the last digits of the count are all even.
<bookmark mark='six'/>But six, ten and fourteen end in even digits, and four does not divide them.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>An even last digit is not enough, so we must look at more of the number.
